items.jobTitle: CDI - HR Data & Social Controlling Analyst H/F
items.jobDescription:
Mission principale 
 Rattachée à la Head of HR Operations, le/la HR Data & Social Controlling Analyst assure le pilotage de la masse salariale et des effectifs, tout en développant une approche analytique et data-driven de la fonction RH. 
 Il/elle garantit la fiabilité des données sociales, contribue à la construction et au suivi du budget RH, automatise les reportings et transforme les données RH en analyses pertinentes en étroite collaboration avec la Direction Financière. 
 Principales responsabilités 
 A. Contrôle de gestion sociale et pilotage de la masse salariale 
 Construire le budget annuel de masse salariale et des effectifs, en lien avec la DRH, la Direction Financière et les équipes opérationnelles. 
 Élaborer les prévisions actualisées (forecasts) et les projections de fin d'année. 
 Analyser les écarts entre réalisé, budget et prévisions, et identifier les principaux facteurs explicatifs. 
 Modéliser les effets des évolutions d'effectifs, des augmentations salariales, des promotions, des bonus, des départs et des recrutements. 
 Réaliser des simulations financières pour accompagner les décisions RH : recrutements, réorganisations, politiques de rémunération et évolution des effectifs. 
 Suivre les principaux indicateurs économiques et sociaux : masse salariale, effectifs, rémunération moyenne, coûts des recrutements et autres coûts RH. 
 Contribuer à l'amélioration des processus de contrôle et de fiabilisation des données de paie et de rémunération. 
 Préparer les analyses nécessaires aux revues budgétaires et aux présentations destinées au CODIR. 
 B. HR Data Analytics et aide à la décision 
 Exploiter et croiser les données issues du SIRH, de la paie, du recrutement et des autres outils RH. 
 Analyser les tendances RH et identifier les principaux facteurs d'évolution des indicateurs sociaux. 
 Réaliser des analyses approfondies sur le turnover, l'absentéisme, le recrutement, la mobilité interne, les rémunérations et les parcours professionnels. 
 Identifier les populations, métiers ou entités nécessitant une attention particulière et formuler des recommandations opérationnelles. 
 Développer des analyses permettant d'évaluer l'efficacité des politiques RH et d'en mesurer les résultats. 
 Concevoir des analyses prospectives et, lorsque les données le permettent, des modèles de prévision pour anticiper les évolutions des effectifs et des indicateurs sociaux. 
 Traduire les résultats des analyses en recommandations compréhensibles et directement exploitables par les équipes RH et les managers. 
 C. Reporting, Business Intelligence et automatisation 
 Concevoir, maintenir et faire évoluer les tableaux de bord RH et les reportings destinés à la DRH, au CODIR et aux équipes opérationnelles. 
 Automatiser la production des reportings récurrents afin de réduire les tâches manuelles et de sécuriser les résultats. 
 Développer des dashboards interactifs permettant de suivre les indicateurs clés et d'analyser les données par métier, entité, pays, population ou niveau hiérarchique. 
 Harmoniser les définitions, les règles de calcul et les référentiels des indicateurs RH. 
 Contribuer à l'amélioration de la qualité, de la cohérence et de la disponibilité des données sociales. 
 Participer à l'évolution des outils de reporting et à l'optimisation des processus de collecte et d'exploitation des données. 
 D. Projets RH 
 Participer activement à l’ensemble des exercices annuels liés aux sujets Comp & Ben : 
 Révision annuelle des salaires, évaluation des bonus, plan de commissionnement pour les équipes de vente. 
 Etudes de rémunérations, benchmarks internes et externes. 
 Profil recherché 
 Formation 
 Bac +5 en contrôle de gestion, finance, statistiques, data analytics, ressources humaines ou école de commerce avec spécialisation pertinente. 
 Une double compétence en finance et en data constitue un atout. 
 Expérience 
 3 à 5 ans d'expérience en contrôle de gestion sociale, HR Analytics, contrôle de gestion ou analyse de données, idéalement avec une exposition aux problématiques RH. 
 Une expérience dans le retail, la mode, le luxe ou un environnement multi-entités est appréciée. 
 Compétences techniques 
 Excellente maîtrise d'Excel et des fonctions avancées d'analyse de données. 
 Bonne maîtrise de Power BI. 
 Capacité à manipuler, consolider et analyser des données provenant de plusieurs systèmes. 
 Bonne compréhension des mécanismes de masse salariale, des rémunérations, des effectifs et des principaux indicateurs sociaux. 
 Capacité à construire des modèles budgétaires, des prévisions et des analyses de sensibilité. 
 La connaissance du système de paie ADP est un avantage. 
 Doté d’un esprit analytique, vous êtes rigoureux et proactif, vous comprenez l’environnement Business, et êtes à l’aise dans la collaboration avec les différents départements. 
 Nous sommes convaincus que la diversité de nos équipes est une force. Nous étudions toutes les candidatures avec la même attention, sans distinction de genre, de handicap, d'origine, d'âge ou d'orientation.

items.jobTitle: Ingénieur Sécurité des Procédés - Process Safety Engineer (H/F)
items.jobDescription:
📜 Contexte 
 Dans le cadre du renforcement de l'équipe Sécurité des Procédés d'un site industriel situé à Genève, Suisse , nous recherchons un(e) Ingénieur(e) Sécurité des Procédés (H/F) afin de contribuer à la maîtrise des risques liés aux procédés chimiques et à la sécurité des opérations industrielles.
 Rattaché(e) au Département HSE / Sécurité des Procédés , vous évoluerez dans un environnement industriel exigeant et apporterez un support technique aux équipes de Production, de Maintenance et d'Ingénierie.
 Votre rôle sera axé sur la prévention des accidents majeurs, la conformité aux standards et réglementations applicables, ainsi que l'amélioration continue de la performance sécurité des procédés du site.
 📌 Votre rôle 
 En tant qu' Ingénieur(e) Sécurité des Procédés , vous interviendrez comme expert(e) technique sur l'ensemble des sujets liés à la sécurité des procédés.
 Vous contribuerez à l'identification, à l'évaluation et à la maîtrise des risques procédés sur les installations existantes, les modifications techniques et les nouveaux projets.
 Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes EHS, Ingénierie, Production et Maintenance , ainsi qu'avec des interlocuteurs externes et les autorités locales lorsque nécessaire.
 Vos missions
 🎯 Responsabilités 
 🔹 Analyse des risques procédés 
• Réaliser et mettre à jour les analyses de risques procédés, notamment les études HAZOP, What-If et LOPA .
• Identifier les scénarios de risques potentiels et recommander les mesures de prévention et de protection adaptées.
• Contribuer aux études de sécurité des installations existantes et des nouveaux projets.
 🔹 Sécurité thermique & analyse technique 
• Interpréter les résultats d'essais de sécurité thermique tels que DSC, C80 et RC1 .
• Identifier des solutions concrètes pour maîtriser les risques liés aux réactions chimiques et aux procédés industriels.
• Analyser des données techniques complexes et formuler des recommandations claires.
 🔹 Ingénierie & projets industriels 
• Participer aux revues de conception des équipements et des installations industrielles.
• Contribuer aux projets d'investissement et aux modifications d'installations sous l'angle de la sécurité des procédés.
• Veiller à la prise en compte des exigences de sécurité tout au long de la conception.
 🔹 Gestion du changement & conformité 
• Participer aux processus de gestion du changement (MOC) .
• Évaluer l'impact sécurité procédés des modifications techniques et vérifier leur conformité aux exigences applicables.
• Soutenir la mise en œuvre et le suivi des standards de sécurité des procédés conformément à la politique EHS de l'entreprise.
 🔹 Support aux opérations & à la maintenance 
• Apporter un support technique aux équipes d'exploitation et de maintenance sur les sujets de sécurité des procédés.
• Apporter votre expertise sur des thématiques telles que l'inertage, les pressions, les températures et les compatibilités chimiques .
• Accompagner les équipes dans la mise en œuvre des bonnes pratiques de sécurité des procédés.
 🔹 Audits, réglementation & études de sécurité 
• Participer aux audits et inspections de conformité réglementaire.
• Contribuer aux analyses quantitatives des risques (QRA) , aux études de protection contre les explosions et aux autres évaluations de sécurité.
• Veiller au respect des standards et réglementations applicables en matière de sécurité des procédés.
 🔹 Formation & sensibilisation 
• Former et sensibiliser le personnel aux principes et bonnes pratiques de sécurité des procédés.
• Promouvoir une culture forte de la sécurité des procédés sur le site.
• Communiquer les exigences réglementaires et techniques aux interlocuteurs concernés.
 Vos compétences
 💼 Votre profil 
 • Diplôme d'ingénieur ou Master en génie chimique, chimie ou domaine équivalent .
• Minimum 5 ans d'expérience en sécurité des procédés dans un environnement industriel chimique ou pharmaceutique.
• Expérience confirmée dans la réalisation d'études de sécurité des procédés.
• Maîtrise des méthodologies HAZOP, LOPA, SIL et ATEX .
• Bonne connaissance des standards internationaux de sécurité des procédés tels que API, CCPS, IEC 61511 et SEVESO .
• Capacité à lire et interpréter des P&ID, schémas de procédé et spécifications d'équipements .
• Fortes capacités d'analyse et de résolution de problèmes, avec l'aptitude à synthétiser des informations techniques complexes.
• Excellentes qualités de communication et capacités pédagogiques.
• Esprit d'équipe, proactivité et autonomie.
• Français courant et bon anglais technique , notamment pour la lecture et la rédaction de documents HSE internationaux.
 Avantages
 🏆 Conditions du poste 
 • 📍 Lieu : Genève, Suisse 
• 🕒 Taux d'activité : 100 % 
• 📅 Date de démarrage : flexible, à convenir 
 ⚠️ Ce poste est ouvert aux candidat(e)s de nationalité suisse ou européenne (UE/AELE), ou titulaires d'un permis de travail valable pour la Suisse.

Role - Software Engineer - Optimisation Team 
 Company - iwell - Harmonizing Clean Energy 
 Location - Utrecht 
 About iwell 
 At iwell, we are all about reinforcing energy security. We help European businesses become more energy independent. With growing regulations, extreme price volatility and rising grid issues, they need to be resilient. It is time to take charge and think ahead. 
 We deliver energy management solutions that ensure that businesses are always in control of their energy. Our in-house developed EMS and modular battery storage drive profit through sustainability, making businesses future-proof.  
 We are a fast-growing international team of bold, talented individuals. From engineers and software developers to creative thinkers and customer-focused business developers. No matter what your strong suit is, we always are looking for people who are determined to make a positive impact. 
 The Role 
 The Optimisation team builds the Python applications that decide what our customers' energy assets should do, and when. Batteries, EV fleets, solar and grid connections all come together in our optimiser, and the team turns prices, forecasts and constraints into schedules and decisions that run in production every day. 
 Much of this work has an operations-research flavour, and the problems rarely arrive neatly defined.. They arrive as a customer who needs their vans charged by 6:00 at the lowest cost or a battery whose value depends on the hour. We're looking for someone who is comfortable across that whole path: understanding the real-world problem, shaping it into something a computer can solve, and shipping and operating the result. You don't need to be an OR specialist. You do need to be a strong Python engineer who enjoys messy, concrete problems. 
 Success in this role means being able to: 
 Take a loosely defined operational problem and turn it into working, maintainable production code. 
 Work with data and models (optimisation, forecasting or plain statistics) without losing sight of the engineering. 
 What you will do 
 Create charging schedules for EV fleets that minimise electricity costs while guaranteeing every vehicle is ready when it needs to be. This means modelling tariffs, grid limits and departure times, and handling what happens when reality deviates from the plan. 
 Calculate the value of each kWh produced or consumed, so that batteries, solar and flexible loads are steered by what energy is actually worth at that moment, and customers can see where their savings come from. 
 Build forecasting models that predict operational issues before they happen, to maximise asset uptime and reduce the number of support tickets our Operations team has to handle. 
 Take your work all the way to production: packaging, deployment, monitoring and bugfixing. 
 Work with the rest of the Optimisation team on the shared tooling, data pipelines and modelling conventions the team uses.. 
 What are looking for 
 5+ years of production Python development experience, writing clean, tested, maintainable code. 
 A proven ability to translate real-world problems into working code. 
 A pragmatic mindset: you choose the boring, well-understood solution when it's the right one, and you know when it isn't. 
 Strong communication skills and a habit of documenting your work. Fluency in English is required. 
 Weekly working hours of 32-40 hours  
 Coming into the office 3-4 days per week 
 Bonus points for 
 None of these are required. We'd rather hire a strong engineer and teach the domain than the other way around. 
 Experience with a modelling library such as cvxpy or Pyomo, or other operations research experience.. 
 Time-series forecasting in production, or basic MLOps: keeping models trained, monitored and honest. 
 Data analysis experience 
 Energy, battery or electricity domain knowledge: tariffs, grid constraints, day-ahead and imbalance markets. 
 The willingness to take on a People lead role in the team. 
 Note: at iwell, we value growth potential over perfection. Feel free to respond if you can see yourself meeting this list in the (near) future. 
 What we offer 
 A competitive salary within the range of EUR 4400-EUR6600 + 8% holiday allowance 
 30 holidays per year, plus an annual company trip of 3 days 
 The opportunity to do volunteer work, by offering 1 volunteer day per year 
 Learning & Development budget of EUR 1,500 per year  
 Attractive pension plan with Brand New Day  
 Working remotely for 2 weeks per year  
 We cover your travel costs, regardless of whether you come by bike, car, or public transport. 
 A mobile phone allowance of EUR 25 per month 
 Additional activities such as a bootcamp, volleyball tournament, company drinks etc. 
 iwell is a family-friendly company and employs many employees with care-taking responsibilities 
 Interested? 
 For more information about iwell, what we do, why we do it, and an overview of our partners, visit https://iwell.eu/ . 
 Our application process 
 Apply. Our People & Culture Team and the hiring manager will review your application and will respond within 2 weeks. 
 Phone screening. Are you a true iweller-in-the-making? We will invite you for an introductory call. 
 Are you the one? You will have two interviews. For the second interview,, you will also be asked to work on a case. 
 Acquisition based on this vacancy is not appreciated.

Studenten opgelet: 
 Stage Finance & Control beschikbaar!  
 Wil jij een kijkje in de keuken van een internationale organisatie? Onderdeel zijn van ons finance team waarbij je leert over diverse finance aspecten? En ben je pro-actief, leergierig en hou je ook wel van een geintje op zijn tijd? Lees dan snel verder! 
 Dit is P1
 P1 Travel is het grootste sportevenementen Ticketing bureau van Europa en wij werken officieel samen met de grootste voetbalclubs, stadions en toernooien ter wereld. Denk aan clubs als Manchester United, Liverpool, FC Barcelona en SSC Napoli, maar ook de Olympische spelen, Formule 1 en Wimbledon. Wij brengen zakelijke en particuliere klanten naar het evenement van hun dromen. Jij kunt hier onderdeel van uitmaken in de vorm van een stage bij ons Finance team.  Feeling met sport en cijfers? Dan wordt deze stage je grootste hobby! 
 Het finance team  
Het zeskoppige finance team, onder leiding van Martijn, draagt met elkaar zorg voor alle financiële processen binnen de organisatie. Zoals je je wellicht kunt voorstellen is de event/travelbranche een dynamisch speelveld waarbij geen dag hetzelfde is. Aan het finance team de taak om in samenwerking met de rest van de organisatie te zorgen voor kloppende cijfers waarop gestuurd kan worden. 
 Finance & Control stage  
 Gedurende je stage zal je compleet onderdeel zijn van het team en zorgen we voor een gevarieerd takenpakket. Je eerste weken staan in het teken van kennismaken met onze processen en werkwijzes. Daarna zul je aan de slag gaan met je eigen takenpakket. Hierbij kun je denken aan: 
 Maken van periodieke en ad hoc rapportages;  
 Meewerken aan financiële maand- en jaarafsluitingen; 
 Uitvoeren van checks en controles op o.a juistheid en volledigheid van financiële data en processen;  
 Maken van resultaatboekingen op events en het analyseren daarvan. 
 Naast het op doen van waardevolle ervaring in de organisatie gaan we graag met je in gesprek over grote en uitdagende projecten die P1 en jou verder helpt in de ontwikkeling. Bijvoorbeeld het zelf opzetten van managementrapportages.  
 Jouw profiel  
 Je volgt momenteel een financiële studie in de richting van Accountancy, Bedrijfseconomie, Bedrijfsadministratie, Finance & Control o.i.d. en bent op zoek naar een meewerkstage per januari/februari 2027. 
 Je bent pro-actief, wil zoveel mogelijk leren en steekt graag de handen uit de mouwen. 
 Je beheerst de Nederlandse taal. 
 Mooi meegenomen als je zelf ook een passie hebt voor sport, dat hebben wij namelijk ook!  
 Waar kom je terecht? 
 We zijn gevestigd in het mooie Leiden en je komt terecht in een gezellig én ambitieus bedrijf waar geen dag hetzelfde is. We bestaan momenteel uit een groep van 80 collega’s en werken elk semester met een leuke groep van stagiaires verdeeld over verschillende afdelingen. Je zult dus zeker niet de enige zijn die van start gaat.  
 Dit krijg jij ervoor terug! 
 Naast een afwisselende stage en goede begeleiding wordt er verder goed voor je gezorgd. Denk hierbij aan een gaaf kantoor voorzien van alle gemakken, verzorgde lunch, sportmogelijkheden en de vetste uitjes met de hele toko. Elke stagiair die wij hebben gehad kijkt terug op een onvergetelijke tijd.

 Wat je gaat doen
 Je werkt elke dag met een gezellig team vol gedreven mensen. We hebben ervaring in business control, accounting, corporate finance, data analytics, fiscaal recht en auditing. Crisp groeit snel, en de verantwoordelijkheden van ons team dus ook. Zo is geen dag hetzelfde en blijven we onszelf continu ontwikkelen. We sparren veel en staan open voor elkaars mening.

 Je beschikt over een afgeronde hbo- of universitaire opleiding (bijvoorbeeld Finance, Bedrijfseconomie of Accountancy).

 Je bent integer, nauwkeurig en risicobewust. Je begrijpt dat een strakke administratie de basis vormt voor goede besluitvorming.

 Werken bij een B Corp gecertificeerd bedrijf, waarbij je de kans krijgt om je stempel te drukken op het Europese voedselsysteem.

Our Mission 
Aleph Alpha is one of the few companies in Europe doing serious foundation model pre-training like our recently released Kolibri-1 model . Our customers - in finance, manufacturing, public administration - need models that understand German, meet European regulatory requirements, and work reliably in high-stakes settings. We're building that in Heidelberg.
 We are hiring an AI Researcher (f/m/d) to join our Pre-training team and help advance the architecture and training of our next generation of foundation models. If you are excited about how large models learn, want to run experiments that feed directly into production training runs, and want hands-on time on large-scale clusters (thousands of NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs), we would love to hear from you.
 Team Culture 
We foster a culture built on ownership, autonomy, and empowerment. Teams and individual contributors are trusted to take responsibility for their work and drive meaningful impact. We maintain a flat organizational structure with efficient, supportive management that enables quick decision-making, open communication, and a strong sense of shared purpose. We collaborate closely on complex technical problems, working in pairs or using mob programming to resolve challenging issues. New team members learn through real work: from your first weeks you will pair with experienced researchers on live problems, and take on more ownership as you grow into it.
 About the Role 
As an AI Researcher in Pre-training (f/m/d) , you will work on the technical levers that determine the success of our next-generation models: architecture, optimization, stability, and scaling.
 Working at the intersection of research and engineering, you will learn to translate mathematical reasoning and empirical observations into principled training decisions, from small-scale proxy experiments to multi-thousand-GPU runs. You will start with well-scoped problems alongside senior researchers and progressively take ownership of larger parts of the training recipe.
 We are looking for someone with strong fundamentals, sharp experimental instincts, exceptional skills, and the drive to go deep fast. You learn as much from a failed run as from a paper, you write code others can build on, and you want to become an expert in large-scale pre-training.
 Your Responsibilities 
 Recipe & Architecture Experiments: Design and run ablations on core elements of the training recipe (optimizers, schedules, initialization), and implement PyTorch-based architectural changes. Evaluate their effect on convergence, stability, and training efficiency.
 Scaling Experiments: Run and analyze small-scale proxy experiments, and contribute to the hyperparameter scaling laws and scale-up methods we use to predict behavior at multi-thousand-GPU scale.
 Run Monitoring & Debugging: Help monitor large-scale training runs and investigate convergence issues such as loss spikes and divergence. Work with the team to track down distributed training failures.
 Research to Practice: Follow the literature, reproduce promising results at small scale, and bring ideas worth testing to the team.
 Cross-Team Collaboration: Work with the Compute Performance, Data, Evaluation, and Post-Training teams to understand how hardware constraints and the rest of the model lifecycle shape pre-training decisions.
 Core Qualifications 
 You are proficient in Python and have hands-on experience with PyTorch.
 You have a strong foundation in machine learning, shown through research (e.g., a PhD, a strong MS'c thesis, or publications), open-source contributions, or substantial professional or substantial personal projects.
 You have a solid mathematical background (linear algebra, probability, optimization) and enjoy reasoning formally about why models train the way they do.
 You understand how transformers work and have pre-trained LLMs from scratch yourself, even at small scale.
 You design experiments carefully, report noisy and negative results honestly, and can explain clearly what your evidence does and does not show.
 You have a track record of picking up unfamiliar technical areas quickly and going deep, for example by reimplementing papers, ramping up on a large new codebase, or debugging a problem well outside your comfort zone.
 You write clean, maintainable code and care about reproducible experiments.

 En juillet 2026, Qonto a racheté Acasi pour construire la première offre bancaire et comptable vraiment intégrée pour les entrepreneurs. Notre conviction : les entrepreneurs méritent une comptabilité certifiée, intégrée directement à leurs outils, pilotée par des pros qui ont du temps pour conseiller plutôt que pour saisir. L'IA automatise ce qui peut l'être, et le métier se déplace vers ce qui a toujours eu le plus de valeur : le conseil et la relation client. 
 En tant que Collaborateur Comptable, tu rejoindras une équipe en hypercroissance au cœur de cette transformation, avec un portefeuille de clients à piloter en autonomie et un rôle actif dans l'évolution de notre solution.
 ➡️ Ce que tu feras 
 Conseil de confiance : Tu es l'interlocuteur principal de tes clients sur leurs enjeux fiscaux, financiers, juridiques et comptables — pas un exécutant, un référent. Parmi tes clients, une variété de dossiers comme des professions libérales, consultants, développeurs, RH indépendants, entreprises d’e-commerce, agents immobiliers ou encore des holdings.
 Pilote ton portefeuille : Tu prends en charge la tenue, la révision et les obligations fiscales de tes clients (TVA, liasses fiscales, dépôt des comptes), avec des outils pensés pour aller vite sur ce qui peut être automatisé.
 Façonne notre produit : Tu es le lien entre tes clients et notre équipe produit. Leurs retours, leurs frustrations, leurs besoins — tu les remontes directement et tu participes à l'évolution de la solution Acasi.
 Contribue aux clôtures : Tu travailles en équipe sur les clôtures comptables périodiques, en veillant à la cohérence et à la fiabilité des comptes.
 ➡️ Ce qu'on recherche 
 Formation comptable : DSCG, Master CCA, ou EC mémorialiste, à n'importe quelle étape de ton parcours.
 Une première expérience en cabinet :  6 mois minimum avec du front-client, en alternance ou en poste. Tu connais le rythme des échéances et sais interagir en direct avec tes clients.
 Appétence pour le digital et l'IA : Tu t'intéresses à ce que la technologie change dans le métier et tu veux travailler dans un cabinet qui en fait un avantage, pas un sujet de peur.
 Organisation et écoute : Tu jongleras avec plusieurs dossiers et plusieurs clients. L'écoute et la rigueur ne sont pas négociables.
 Envie de construire quelque chose : Acasi n'est pas un cabinet figé. Tu veux participer à ce qui se construit — pas juste occuper un poste.
 Langues : français courant indispensable pour la relation client. Anglais B1 minimum — nos équipes et nos outils sont en partie en anglais.
 ➡️ Ce qu'on t'offre 
 Être au cœur du réacteur : L'IA va transformer la comptabilité plus vite que n'importe quel autre secteur. Chez Acasi, tu n'observes pas cette transformation depuis les gradins — tu en es l'un des acteurs.
 Un rôle produit rare : Tu as une voix directe sur l'évolution d'un logiciel comptable utilisé par des milliers de clients. Peu de cabinets offrent ça.
 Autonomie réelle dès l'arrivée : Ton portefeuille est à toi. La taille et la complexité s'adaptent à ton niveau — mais la responsabilité, elle, est immédiate.
 Une rémunération compétitive : un salaire fixe à 40 000€ brut/an, associé à une prime à la performance pendant la période fiscale — parce qu'on sait que les bons profils ont le choix.

About EH Energy Engineering 
 EH Energy is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy-duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product delivers a significantly more compact fuel cell system with high power density and lower production costs. In response to the challenges of climate change and the global shift toward decentralized energy, EH Energy provides high-performance, cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.
 To support our rapid growth and bring our systems to global markets, we are seeking a Certification Engineer. In this critical role, you will take full ownership of our product compliance roadmap, bridging the gap between innovative engineering and strict global regulations. You will lead hazard and risk assessments, define certification strategies across international markets (EU, North America, marine), and interface directly with notified bodies and classification societies to ensure our fuel cell systems are safe, fully compliant, and market-ready.
 This role requires a full-time, on-site presence at our office in Nyon, Switzerland . We are unable to offer remote or hybrid arrangements , so candidates should be based locally or prepared to relocate .
   Key responsibilities 
 Certification strategy and project management 
 Identify applicable directives, regulations, harmonised standards and class rules early in the development cycle and translate them into design requirements (EU, North America, marine)
 Select and manage notified bodies, NRTLs, classification societies and test laboratories, own budgets, schedules and contracts for certification work
 Plan and witness type tests, factory acceptance tests (FAT) and site acceptance tests (SAT)
 Safety engineering and risk analysis 
 Lead risk assessments to ISO 12100 and hazard studies (HAZID, HAZOP to IEC 61882)
 Lead design and process FMEA (IEC 60812) for stacks, balance of plant, containers and fuel processing
 Run explosion-protection assessments: hazardous area classification (IEC 60079-10-1), ventilation and gas detection concepts, and equipment selection
 Specify and verify safety functions to ISO 13849 (PL) and IEC 61508, including safety requirement specifications and validation reports
 Compliance and technical documentation 
 Compile and maintain technical construction files, CE Declarations of Conformity, type-approval dossiers and certification reports
 Write and review user, installation, operation and maintenance manuals, safety instructions and labelling
 Maintain the standards register and assess the impact of new or revised standards
 Manage certification change control: assess design changes for impact on existing certificates
 Collaboration and continuous improvement 
 Act as the internal authority on certification scope: ensure in-service conformity of series production with certified designs, and support procurement and supply chain on material and packaging compliance (e.g. RoHS, packaging regulations).
 Support design reviews and supplier qualification, including component certificates (ATEX, PED, electrical)
 Standards and regulatory scope 
 The role covers, but is not limited to, the frameworks below. Working knowledge of most is expected; deep expertise in several is required
 IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1:2021, ISO 16110-1 and Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230
 Required qualifications 
 Master’s or bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, chemical, process or safety engineering, or equivalent
 5+ years in product certification, compliance or safety engineering for complex electromechanical or process equipment (energy, gas, process, machinery or marine)
 Direct experience with hydrogen or fuel cell systems and the IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1 or ISO 16110
 Proven track record of taking products through CE marking and third-party certification with notified bodies or NRTLs
 Hands-on experience leading FMEA, HAZOP and risk assessments, and documenting them to auditor standard
 Solid knowledge of ATEX / IECEx, hazardous area classification and explosion-protection concepts
 Experience specifying and validating safety functions to ISO 13849 and/or IEC 61508
 Excellent technical writing: clear, structured, audit-ready technical files and manuals
 Fluent English, written and spoken
 Preferred qualifications and personal profile 
 Nice to have 
 Marine type approval with a classification society (DNV, LR, BV, ABS) or IGF Code projects
 Experience with fuel processing, reformers or fire equipment, and with pressure equipment under PED
 Certified functional safety qualification or ATEX/IECEx competence certification
 Familiarity with North American codes (NEC, NFPA) and UL/CSA certification
 Personal profile 
 Rigorous and structured, with a strong safety mindset and an eye for detail
 Pragmatic: finds compliant solutions that keep development moving
 Confident communicator with engineers, auditors, authorities and customers
 Self-driven in a fast-growing, scale-up environment; comfortable owning topics end to end
 Start date: Immediately

items.jobTitle: Product Safety & Certification Engineer - Fuel Cell Systems
items.jobDescription:
About EH Energy Engineering 
 EH Energy is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product is a significantly more compact fuel cell with high power density and lower costs of production. Faced with the challenges of climate change and the transition to a decentralised energy system, EHG seeks to provide high performance and cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.
 To help achieve our vision of a decarbonised future we are seeking a Functional Safety Engineer to embed safety into our fuel cell systems, leading hazard analysis and safety engineering across hardware, software and controls to ensure our products are safe, compliant and certifiable.
 This role requires full-time, on-site presence at our Nyon, Switzerland office. We're not able to offer remote or hybrid arrangements, so candidates should be prepared to relocate.
   Key Responsibilities: 
 • Own the functional safety lifecycle for fuel cell systems from concept to release
 • Lead hazard and risk analyses (HARA, HAZOP, FMEA/FMEDA, FTA) and define safety goals
 • Derive safety requirements and concepts and allocate them across hardware, software and controls
 • Define/verify safety mechanisms, diagnostics and safe states with the controls and embedded teams
 • Perform safety analyses and calculations (SIL/PL/ASIL determination, metrics, PFH/PFD)
 • Compile safety cases, safety plans and supporting documentation for certification
 • Interface with notified bodies, certification authorities and customers on safety topics
 • Promote a strong safety culture and coach teams on functional safety practices
   Skills and Experience Required: 
 • BSc/MSc in electrical, electronic, mechatronic, control or safety engineering is mandatory
 • Minimum 3-5 years of functional safety experience in industrial, energy or hydrogen systems
 • Working knowledge of safety standards (ex. IEC 61508, ISO 13849, ISO 26262 and/or IEC 62061)
 • Hands-on experience with HARA, FMEA/FMEDA, FTA and safety requirements engineering
 • Understanding of safety-related hardware, embedded software and control architectures
 • Familiarity with hydrogen, high-voltage or pressure system safety is a strong plus
 • Team player able to work autonomously with internal and external experts
 • Excellent spoken and written English is mandatory; French/German is a plus
 • Functional safety certification (e.g. TÜV FSEng) is a plus
   Start date: Immediately

WHO WE ARE 🌍
 Creating content that resonates is great — turning that attention into growth is even better. That's what Manychat does.
 Our AI-powered automations help creators and brands engage with audiences across Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp, and TikTok — at the right moment, with the right message, minus the manual work.
 We're 400+ people across three continents behind the leading platform for conversational growth, with AI skills shaping how we build, how we work, and how we grow.
 WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR 🚀 🌟
 Want to shape an AI platform's architecture from day one, instead of just maintaining what someone else built?
 Manychat runs AI features for businesses worldwide, and we're hiring an SRE to own the reliability, performance, and cost of that AI infrastructure, and to raise the bar for how our whole engineering org builds on LLMs.
 This isn't a classical SRE role with a bit of AI sprinkled on top. We need someone AI-native: you already understand how modern LLM systems behave in production, things like token throughput, provider rate limits, degraded model quality, and inference latency tails, and you treat all of that as a first-class reliability concern, not an afterthought.
 Why this role is worth your time:
 The AI Platform is still young, so you'll shape its architecture, standards, and roadmap from the ground up.
 The stakes are real. AI features sit right in the critical path of customer-facing automation, so your work actually matters to the business, not just to a dashboard.
 You'll partner directly with the Head of Infrastructure, with real autonomy and visibility into how your decisions play out.
 Sound like the kind of ownership you've been looking for?
 WHAT YOU'LL DO 🚀
 Own reliability and performance of our AI infrastructure: AI Gateway, inference services, and integrations with Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and other LLM providers.
 Design and evolve the AI Gateway: routing, failover between providers, rate limiting, caching, and guardrails.
 Build observability for AI systems: latency/throughput/error SLOs per model and provider, token-level metrics, quality and drift signals.
 Drive cost optimization and FinOps for AI workloads: per-feature cost visibility, model right-sizing, caching strategies, provider mix.
 Run capacity planning and incident response for inference services; write and improve runbooks and postmortems.
 Scale AI expertise across the org: set standards, review designs, and coach teams shipping LLM-backed features.
 TO SHINE IN THIS ROLE 💥
 You’ll need:
 5+ years in SRE / platform / infrastructure engineering, including production ownership at significant scale.
 Hands-on experience operating LLM-backed systems in production: provider APIs (Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar), inference pipelines, self-hosted or managed model serving.
 Deep cloud-native background: AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform/IaC, CI/CD.
 Strong observability practice (Prometheus/Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or equivalent) and experience defining SLOs for non-deterministic systems.
 Proven cost-optimization work: you can show where you cut cloud or inference spend and how you made cost visible.
 Staff-level influence: you've set technical direction beyond your own team and brought others along
 It would be great if you have:
 Experience building or operating an LLM gateway/proxy (e.g., LiteLLM, Kong AI Gateway, custom).
 Experience with GPU workload optimization, quantization, or serving frameworks (vLLM, TGI, Triton).
 Experience with eval pipelines and quality monitoring for LLM outputs.
 Why this role
 Green-field ownership: the AI Platform is young; you'll shape its architecture, standards, and roadmap.
 Real scale and real stakes: AI features sit in the critical path of customer-facing automation.
 Direct partnership with the Head of Infrastructure; high autonomy and visibility.
 WHAT WE OFFER 🤗
 We care deeply about your growth, well-being, and comfort:
 🌍 Hybrid onboarding to start work remotely and relocation support for you and your family.
 💙 Comprehensive health insurance for both you and your family.
 📚 Professional development budget for conference tickets, online courses, and other relevant resources to help you grow.
 🫶 Flexible benefits package: no one-size-fits-all perks here. You get a budget and you decide where it goes, from health and wellbeing to family and setting up your home office.
 🪴 Hybrid work and generous, flexible time off — planned with your team, not rationed by a rigid quota.
 🍽️ In-office perks, including free meals and snacks.
 🤝 Company-funded sport activities, annual offsites and team-building events.
 🤖 AI isn't a perk here — it's how we work. Claude, OpenAI, and more are on by default from day one, and we back teams in adopting whatever makes them faster.

 Experience working within an EASA Part 21J Design Organisation or international equivalent.
 Practical experience with the design and integration of aircraft powerplant systems. Experience with electric aviation or electric propulsion systems is an asset.

 Sound knowledge of mechanical component design, aerospace materials, standard hardware and manufacturing methods, including geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, assembly and inspection requirements.

 Ability to develop and assess installation designs while balancing functional, structural, environmental, certification, manufacturing and maintainability considerations.
 Experience collaborating with external development partners, engineering service providers or aerospace suppliers.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a methodical approach and attention to detail.
 A high degree of self-motivation, resilience, reliability and precision, combined with a strong sense of ownership.
 Collaborative team player with a positive attitude and the ability to work effectively in a multicultural team.
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English; proficiency in another European language is an asset.
 Passionate about aviation and the electrification of the aviation industry.

 Pension scheme to support your long-term financial security.

items.jobDescription:
wingmaite captures the knowledge companies never write down: who decides what, how work actually gets done, and why decisions were made. Our AI agents use that knowledge to answer questions and get work done.
 We're looking for a Staff engineer to own the technical quality and direction of our agent platform. You'll build features end to end, from the agent into the backend. You won't manage people. You'll work closely with our CTO as a technical sparring partner.
 What You'll Do
 Design the agents: Decide how our agents plan, use tools and handle multi-step work, and where people need to step in. Build reusable components so each new use case doesn't need its own system.
 Connect agents to company knowledge: Build how that knowledge reaches the agents, together with the people who decide what it should contain.
 Make answers reliable: Agents should be correct, cite their sources, show people only what they're allowed to see, and know when not to act.
 Track quality: Build evals, monitor quality and cost, and keep our model choices up to date.
 Ship end to end: Build features from the agent through to the backend yourself.
 Keep the architecture consistent: Set the patterns others build on, document decisions, keep specs current, and review designs with engineering, product and design.
 How We Work
 We build features as one team: design, product, engineering and AI together, from the first idea to production. You'll help shape a feature while it's still a problem and stay with it until it works for users. Agents depend on the knowledge behind them, so we build both as one system. We write decisions down and discuss disagreements openly.
 What This Role Is Not
 A management role, a prompt-engineering role, or an infrastructure or security role.
 What We're Looking For
 Must-Haves 
 You've shipped multi-step, tool-using LLM agents to production (LangGraph or similar)
 You know when sub-agents help, how to build good evals, and why retrieval fails
 Fluent in Python and productive in TypeScript/Node (NestJS is a plus)
 PostgreSQL and data modeling
 You use AI coding tools such as Claude Code every day
 You write clear specs and can explain trade-offs to people who aren't engineers
 Fluent English (C1–C2)
 Nice-to-Haves 
 None of these are required, but they'll help you get up to speed faster:
 You've connected agents to tools and data through MCP 
 You've worked with knowledge graphs or other ways of modeling how people, work and information relate
 You've run models in production on AWS Bedrock or Vertex AI 
 You've traced and debugged agents with LLM observability tools such as Langfuse
 You speak German 
 Who You Are
 You've set technical direction beyond your own work, and others build on your patterns
 You start from what users need and what could go wrong, then choose the tools
 You care whether the system still makes sense in a year
 You're happy to do backend work when a feature needs it
 You want influence through your work, not through a title
 You like working with designers and product people
 You enjoy technical debate and change your mind when the other argument is better
 What We Offer
 Flexible remote setup
 Learning & development opportunities
 Generous vacation & workation budget
 Technical ownership of the platform at the core of wingmaite's product
 How to Apply
 Upload your CV through join and fill in the questionnaire so we can consider your application for the role! Optional: a link to agent or eval work you're proud of.

Role : Founding Design Engineer (Senior / Staff)
 Company : CodeSpeak
 Location : London, on-site. Ideally you already live in London. Candidates based elsewhere are welcome to apply, and remote is possible for a very strong candidate, but UK-based candidates come first. Candidates with a Global Talent visa, granted or in process, are a good fit.
 Job Type : Full-time
 About CodeSpeak
 Agents write more code every month. Human brains stay the same. CodeSpeak is building a program model that sits one level above code, so people can see how a program works and changes over time without reading much of it. The goal is to give control back to the developer: you think about architecture, and the routine goes away.
 CodeSpeak was founded by Andrey Breslav, the creator of Kotlin, which millions of developers use daily. Around him is a team that has built the tools other engineers rely on, at Google, Databricks, Perplexity, JetBrains, Sourcegraph, and Elastic. When it comes to program analysis and developer tooling, these are some of the best people in the world. CodeSpeak is backed by Accel and by funds that also invested in Hugging Face and Mistral, and funding covers several years.
 Here is the open problem. The team has a fair idea of what the program model should look like. It does not yet know how to visualise it. As Founding Design Engineer you will decide how it looks, then build it and ship it. The core engineering team has just been hired, and nobody on it has design-engineering skills. You are the missing piece.
 CodeSpeak is a UK company. It has no business in Russia and no ties to Russian companies. It is still testing which problems it can solve best, so priorities may shift.
 What you are expected to do:
 Design and delivery 
 Own how people interact with CodeSpeak: in the CLI, on the web and on any future platform.
 Design the interfaces yourself. Build many prototypes, decide on the right UX and ship the result.
 Harden the prototypes users liked, so they hold up on real data, with the same care for performance and product quality as for design.
 Ship features to production without help from the rest of the team.
 Product problems 
 CodeSpeak works with unusually complex information: developer intent, requirements, code, architecture, the relationships between them, how they change over time, contradictions and dependencies. The job is not to display it, but to help developers understand it, navigate it and act on it.
 Find a way to visualise CodeSpeak's new, higher-level program model.
 In your first 30 days, visualise the architecture of a codebase split into components. Go deeper from there: a single component, its diff and its code review.
 Then interfaces that let developers navigate structured requirements and how they relate to each other, review requirements alongside code review, see how requirements map onto parts of the codebase, explore how intent, architecture and code change over time, browse agent sessions, find contradictions between requirements, and edit and reorganise requirements rather than only view them.
 Web UI is the simplest and most obvious platform. Some of this will live in the console. VS Code plugins and other desktop frameworks may follow, and the final scope is still open.
 Ways of working 
 Find tasks and clarify requirements without waiting for a brief. Nobody will micromanage you. Egor and Andrey give general direction.
 Work directly with the founder and the engineering team to turn early ideas and hypotheses into intuitive, interactive product experiences.
 Take part in design meetings, where many decisions are made on the spot.
 Explain and defend your design decisions to Egor and Andrey. Both hold strong opinions, and both argue hard.
 Argue for your tasks, and step back with good grace if the team disagrees.
 What you need to succeed:
 Craft 
 You can design an interface, prototype it and ship it to production on your own.
 You have strong design taste, and your portfolio shows it: UX, interaction design, information architecture and visual hierarchy. For this role the portfolio is critical.
 You make complex information or a complex data model easy to read. Think maps with metadata or dense dashboards, with non-trivial state. Tools that read and write count for more than infographics or landing pages.
 You have solid computer science and software engineering fundamentals, plus TypeScript, and deep experience building production apps with modern UI frameworks such as React. At least 3 years of delivering production software.
 You understand the problems of engineers, because engineers are CodeSpeak's users.
 How you work 
 You can say why you made each design choice. "I'm an artist, I see it this way" will not work here.
 You are curious and self-directed, and you care about making programming better. You gather requirements and find projects yourself.
 You actively improve your own workflow with AI-powered coding tools.
 You work hard and can be reached when a task needs it. The team has no weekend-work culture.
 You think fast and explain your reasoning clearly.
 You speak Russian, which is the team's working language. This is a priority, not a hard rule, and a strong candidate without Russian will still be considered.
 Nice to have 
 A background as a frontend engineer with good taste. Engineers from SwiftUI, desktop, mobile or full-stack are welcome if they visualise complex things very well.
 Experience with complex data visualisation.
 Some sense of what an early-stage startup is like. A big-tech engineer who knows what they are joining can fit, and so can a former co-founder.
 A technical degree is not required. Self-taught people and people with degrees in geology or biology have done well in roles like this.
 What you get:
 An unsolved problem with real room for your taste. The team is inventing a new way to represent programs, and you decide how it looks.
 A boutique team of strong engineers, built carefully, who have built developer tools at Google, Databricks, Perplexity, JetBrains, Sourcegraph and Elastic.
 An ML team of four, led by Emeli Dral. She co-founded Evidently, an evals startup, and co-authored a very popular Coursera course for data scientists.
 Day-to-day work with Egor, Andrey and the tech lead.
 Backing from Accel and from funds that also invested in Hugging Face and Mistral, with funding for several years.
 A UK contract with a pension and medical insurance.
 Autonomy. You set your own tasks and nobody hovers over you.
 Work in AI, a field most people want to be in.

 Jouw rol 
Bij Heras krijg je de kans om als stagiair bij te dragen aan het Nimble-programma: een strategisch verbeterprogramma gericht op het vereenvoudigen en automatiseren van bedrijfsprocessen. Als stagiair werk je aan het verbeteren van processen binnen domeinen zoals sales, projecten in nieuwbouw en finance. Je analyseert hoe processen vandaag werken en vertaalt dit naar slimme oplossingen met behulp van Power BI en Power Automate. Je levert concrete procesverbeteringen, procesbeschrijvingen, automatiseringen en Power BI dashboards voor operationele en financiële sturing aan alsmede werkende Power Automate flows. Tenslotte lever je een meetbare bijdrage aan efficiëntie (bijv. tijdbesparing of minder fouten).
 Jouw werkzaamheden 
 In kaart brengen van huidige processen en knelpunten.
 Automatiseren van handmatige processen met Power Automate.
 Ontwikkelen van dashboards en rapportages in Power BI (zonder daadwerkelijk programmeren).
 Verbeteren van datakwaliteit en inzicht in KPI’s.
 Samenwerken met business teams en IT-specialisten.

 Wie zijn wij? 
Heras is een vooraanstaand Europese totaalleverancier van permanente perimeter protection oplossingen. Wij opereren vanuit meer dan 24 landen en hebben meer dan 1100 hoogopgeleide experts in dienst. Opgericht in 1952, vervult en overtreft Heras de beveiligingsbehoeften van klanten in heel Europa. Het is dankzij deze staat van dienst, samen met het blijvend groeiende vakmanschap van onze medewerkers, dat wij ons experts in perimeter protection kunnen noemen. 
 Onze cultuur, werksfeer & waarden 
Wij hebben binnen Heras een informele, open en toegankelijke cultuur. We zijn trots op ons werk, producten en dienstverlening. We hebben een no-nonsense mentaliteit, tonen ondernemerschap, zijn energiek en werken allemaal gedisciplineerd volgens de drie kernwaarden; betrokkenheid, betrouwbaarheid en deskundigheid. Heras is gewaardeerd op een Ecovadis Zilveren Ster en dat plaatst ons bij de duurzaamste 15% bedrijven van Nederland.  Je hebt basiskennis van of affiniteit met Power BI en/of Power Automate
 Je bent analytisch, proactief en communicatief sterk

 Hoewel het niet zelf programmeren beterft vindt je het wel leuk om zelf oplossingen te verzinnen en te testen

About Us: 
 Tebi is creating the first Connected Restaurant Management System that makes hospitality flow. In one seamless platform, Tebi embeds sales, reservations, kitchen prep, payments, and all the data that powers it, creating smooth service and intuitive insights.
Founded by Arnout Schuijff, co-founder of Adyen, and backed by €50 million in funding from Index Ventures & CapitalG, Tebi is built in service of hospitality first. Thousands of restaurants, cafés, bars, and coffee shops across the Netherlands, UK, Italy, Spain, Germany, Denmark and Finland already love running on Tebi.
   About the role: 
 We’re looking for a Senior AI Engineer to build and run the agents at the heart of Tebi OS. You’ll design, ship, evaluate and scale our Product Agents, along with the data pipelines, tools and infrastructure that make them reliable in production.
 The ideal candidate started in data or ML engineering and has since moved into AI engineering, building LLM-powered agents for real users. You enjoy turning messy financial and operational data into context an agent can reason over and act on with confidence and you are passionate about solving product challenges through AI.
 You’ll work closely with product and engineering to put intelligence into the hands of hospitality teams. That could be an agent that answers questions about a restaurant’s finances in real time, one that automates repetitive back-office tasks, or internal tools that help us move faster.
 What you’ll do: 
 Design, build and operate production agents: orchestration, tool and function calling, memory, multi-step reasoning, and integration with Tebi’s backend services
 Build the data foundations agents rely on, including real-time and batch pipelines over financial and operational data, retrieval layers, and well-modeled datasets agents can query safely and accurately
 Turn APIs and internal services into well-defined agent tools, and own the contracts between agents and the rest of the platform
 Set up evaluation for agent behavior: offline eval sets, LLM-as-judge and human review, regression testing on prompt and model changes, and feedback loops that improve agents over time
 Own observability for agents in production by tracing sessions, tool calls and model calls, and tracking latency, cost, error rates and quality
 Work with product teams to find where agents can meaningfully improve the customer experience or internal workflows, and say clearly where they can’t
 Make sure agents handle data securely and responsibly, with sensible guardrails, access controls, and protection against prompt injection and data leakage
 What you’ll bring: 
 7+ years in software engineering, with a solid base in data or ML engineering
 Hands-on experience building and shipping LLM agents to production, not just prototypes. You’ve dealt with flaky tool calls, runaway loops, hallucinated arguments and token budgets, and you have opinions on how to handle them.
 Strong data modeling and data warehousing fundamentals, plus experience with ingestion, transformation and data quality
 Strong SQL, and experience with pipeline tools (e.g. Airflow, dbt) and analytical or cloud data platforms (e.g. ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake)
 Experience evaluating and monitoring LLM systems, and an understanding of the full lifecycle from experiment to deployment to ongoing improvement
 Backend engineering skills: you’re comfortable building the API endpoint that exposes an agent’s output to the frontend, or the service an agent calls as a tool
 Clear communication, including the ability to explain trade-offs in latency, cost, accuracy and complexity to product partners
 A product mindset. You care about how your work lands with users, and you’re keen to meet customers face to face to understand their needs.
 This probably isn't the role for you if you have been working with AI agents to improve your day to day working flows but you haven’t built an Agent in the production.

 The role 
 As Embedded Engineer you own everything between the instrument hardware and our acquisition software.  Design the trigger and acquisition architecture that synchronizes camera exposure, stage motion and laser pulses.

 Your profile

 ~5 years of hands-on experience integrating and controlling hardware, preferably in high-tech equipment, scientific instruments or industrial automation.
 Strong C/C++ and Python, including working with vendor SDKs and drivers on Windows and Linux.
 Proven experience with hardware triggering and synchronization of multiple devices (cameras, motion, lasers, DAQ).
 Experience with FPGA development or working closely with FPGA-based timing hardware.
 Solid grasp of hardware interfaces and networking: Ethernet, USB, serial, PCIe, and multi-device lab networks.
 Comfortable in the lab: reading schematics, using an oscilloscope and logic analyzer, and debugging where hardware and software meet.

 Full professional proficiency in English.

 Bonus 
 Experience with machine-vision cameras, frame grabbers or high-throughput image acquisition.
 Experience with precision motion controllers and encoder-based position triggering.
 High-speed data paths to a host PC, SoC FPGAs or Linux driver development.
 Experience building lightweight web or API layers for instrument control and live data.
 Background in optics, lasers, coherent imaging, semiconductor metrology or lithography equipment.
 Experience with CI, hardware-in-the-loop testing, or working in a Scrum team.
 What we offer

items.jobTitle: Ph.D. Researcher. Knowledge Discovery: From Unstructured Data to Shared Cognitive Maps
items.jobDescription:
Constructor University in collaboration with Constructor Knowledge Labs and Constructor Technology
 About the Position
 The research group led by Prof. Dr. Andrey Ustyuzhanin at Constructor University, in collaboration with Constructor Knowledge Labs (CKL) and Constructor Technology (industry partner), invites applications for Ph.D. student positions in the field of Computer Science, with a focus on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML).
 This PhD position is part of an initiative to advance knowledge representation and adaptive reasoning systems. The research will focus on developing flexible frameworks for actionable knowledge representation that support storage, retrieval, and dynamic adaptation of information across diverse tasks.
 Key objectives include: 
 Transforming unstructured data into interactive knowledge graphs and personalized cognitive maps.
 Designing models that provide interpretable, persistent, and navigable structures of knowledge.
 Addressing challenges such as hierarchy, composability, and coarse-graining for robust, task-specific reasoning.
 Exploring individual and community-level knowledge modeling, including personalized domain maps, profile extraction from artifacts (e.g., papers, courses), and cross-domain abstraction.
 The overarching goal is to create systems that enable transparent, adaptive, and spatially intuitive representations of knowledge , supporting both individual users and collaborative communities.
 Applicant Profile
 Mandatory requirements:
 Holding recognized MSc degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, AI, ML, or a related discipline.
 Students holding BSc degree and exhibiting outstanding performance and extraordinary potential can apply for fast-track PhD.
 Strong mathematical background supported with experience in defining and developing knowledge-graph or information retrieval systems.
 Hands-on experience with large language models (LLMs) and their applications.
 A track record of publications in AI/ML or related areas.
 Documented experience in practical research work.
 Strong skills in academic English writing (peer-reviewed papers, reports, or equivalent).
 Funding & Appointment Terms
 The appointment provides full financial coverage through a dedicated fellowship, comprising:
 Monthly stipend of €1,650
 Monthly research-cost allowance of €100 (Forschungskostenpauschale)
 Health-insurance subsidy of €100 per month
 Supplementary €550 mini-job allowance to support parallel part-time employment (optional)
 Application Details
 Expected start date: September , 2026 
 Application package must include: 
 Curriculum Vitae (CV);
 Academic transcripts ;
 A detailed letter of motivation outlining research interests and career goals;
 2 recommendation letters;
 Applications to be reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisted candidates  will be invited to interviews.

About Clear Street 
 Clear Street’s mission is to give every sophisticated investor access to every asset, in every market, through a unified platform built for speed, transparency and scale. 
 We give our clients the technology, tools, and service once reserved for the largest institutions, rebuilt with modern infrastructure. Our single, cloud-native, end-to-end capital markets platform powers investor growth today and is transforming how they can interact with markets tomorrow. 
 For more information, visit https://clearstreet.io . 
 The Role 
 As a Software Engineer on Clear Street’s Payments team, you’ll play a key role in scaling and modernising our rapidly evolving global payments infrastructure. You’ll develop highly reliable, API-driven systems that integrate seamlessly with external banks and payment gateways, streamlining complex operational workflows and supporting our expansion into new lines of business, including digital initiatives. Working closely with cross-functional partners, you’ll contribute to large-scale, high-impact initiatives that enhance our core payments offering, significantly reduce manual operational processes, and offer our customers a smooth payment experience, helping to shape the future of the Clear Street financial ecosystem. 
 What You’ll Do 
 Engineer highly reliable, API-driven payment systems that streamline operations and support our global expansion. 
 Translate product and design requirements into clean, maintainable and well-tested components. 
 Collaborate closely with product managers, business, operations, designers and back-end engineers to deliver high-quality experiences. 
 Identify and resolve performance, accessibility, and usability issues across the application. 
 Participate in code reviews, contribute to shared component libraries, and help uphold our engineering standards. 
 Support the operational health of your features and help maintain a high SLA. 
 The Team 
 You will work with a team of talented, passionate and highly collaborative engineers. Working together, we have built a platform that serves institutional clients and is at the forefront of technological innovation. Our engineers take pride in not just the value we provide our customers but the quality of our work. You will have the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technologies, collaborate with colleagues from diverse backgrounds, and make a meaningful impact on the financial industry. We value creativity, innovation, strong work ethics, and we are committed to providing our team members with the support and resources they need to succeed. 
 Tech Stack 
 Java Spring Boot, Kafka, gRPC/REST, Kubernetes and Cloud (AWS or Azure). 
 What We’re Looking For 
 Master Java and Spring Boot, and comfortably make tweaks in TypeScript/React, Go, and Python. 
 A proven track record of driving technical decisions and owning complex, large-scale engineering problems end-to-end. 
 Hands-on experience building scalable architectures utilizing Kafka and Kubernetes for robust, resilient integrations. 
 Solid understanding of global payment ecosystems, external banking APIs, and streamlining complex operational workflows. 
 Strong command of software design patterns, distributed systems, clean code principles, and automated testing strategies. 
 Ability to actively manage technical debt, negotiate requirements, and ship reliable solutions without demanding perfection. 
 Actively advocate for better tooling, overhaul inefficient processes, and push our engineering practices forward. 
 A highly collaborative mindset with a preference for collectively solving intricate architectural challenges. 
 "Don't meet every single requirement? Apply anyway! We are looking for strong engineers with a growth mindset, not perfect resumes. If this role excites you, we want to hear from you."  
 What We Offer

Our belief has always been that we are better as a business when we are all together in person. As such, we require employees to be in the office a minimum of three days per week. 
 Our top priority is our people. We’re continuously investing in a culture that promotes collaboration. We help each other through challenges and celebrate each other’s successes. We believe that modern workplaces succeed by virtue of having high-performance workforces that are diverse in ideas, in cultures, and in experiences.  We crawl the web continuously and cannot keep all of it, refresh all of it, or spend a GPU on all of it. Something has to decide which pages are worth indexing, which links are worth following, which pages say the same thing as pages we already have, what has gone stale, and what we should never have picked up. These decisions are worth more than most ranking work. The cheapest way to improve search is to stop indexing pages nobody should ever retrieve, and to start indexing the ones we are missing. Today they run on a mix of learned signals and thresholds someone picked.
 We are looking for a research engineer to own the signals behind those decisions, and the decisions themselves.

 You like working across teams. Crawling, indexing and retrieval all consume what you build
 You care about the problem of finding high quality knowledge and recognize how important this is for the world
 Example Projects 
 Make parsing work on the pages where it currently does not, and prove the improvement rather than assert it
 Teach a model to judge page quality, and get everyone to agree on what quality means well enough to supervise it
 Work on credibility and misinformation as a modelling problem: what a page claims, whether it is a reliable source of it, and whether it was written for a reader or for a crawler
 Decide whether two documents are semantically the same or genuinely different, so we can deduplicate the web without collapsing pages that a user would want to see separately

items.jobTitle: Software Engineer, Knowledge Engine – Query Engine
items.jobDescription:
Exa is an applied AI lab building a search engine unlike the world has ever seen. We build massive-scale infra to crawl the entire web, train state-of-the-art embedding models to process it, and design super high performant vector databases to retrieve over it. We now power search for Cursor, Cognition, HubSpot, and over 400,000 developers and have raised $350m from Lightspeed, Benchmark, and a16z.
 Our ultimate goal is to build perfect search over all the world's information, far beyond Google. If you want to build massive-scale ML systems that will define the way the new AI world consumes information, this is the place for you.
 The Knowledge Platform team builds Exa's knowledge engine. We continuously synthesize information from across the web and beyond into one of the world's largest open-domain knowledge graphs, with hundreds of billions of evidence-backed claims. The work has two halves: construction pipelines that decide what to trust, and retrieval engines that decide how best to search it. Our goal is to give agents answers to any factual question about the world with unprecedented precision and completeness.
 In this role, you'll own the query engine that searches hundreds of billions of claims across a variety of retrieval backends, from a distributed graph database to vector, full-text, time-series and geospatial indexes.
 This is greenfield work with a massive scope. No off-the-shelf system answers precise questions over hundreds of billions of evidence-backed claims at agent speed, so you'll make foundational decisions, from storage layout and indexing across engines to the query language and the planner that routes work between them, that every query depends on.
 What you'll do
 Own storage and indexing across backends: data layout, partitioning and indexes for graph, vector, full-text, time-series and geospatial retrieval, with bulk snapshot builds and live ingest that never take the system down.
 Decide how best to search: cost-based planning from cardinality estimates that chooses, for each question, which backends to use, in what order and how to join their results, executed as traversals, retrievals, filters and aggregations in one plan.
 Make it fast at scale: serve thousands of queries per second, profiling and cutting p50/p99 latency, memory and cost per query under high concurrent load, from on-disk layout to network fan-out.
 Keep answers consistent while the data converges: the graph is fed by live updates and bulk snapshots at once and is eventually consistent by design, so you'll own what a query may see while it converges: consistent snapshot promotion, ordered application of live updates and stable pagination across versions.
 Measure precision and completeness: end-to-end checks every deployment must pass, plus evals and metrics that show when a plan returns wrong results or misses ones it should have found.
 What we're looking for
 You've worked deep inside a distributed database, query engine, search engine or storage system.
 Strong grasp of indexing, query planning and optimization, and storage formats.
 Solid grasp of distributed systems fundamentals: consensus, replication, sharding and fault tolerance.
 Strong in a systems language (Go, Rust or C++).
 You profile before you optimize, and you've shipped measured latency wins in production.
 You obsess over correctness, reliability and data quality as much as scale.
 Bonus
 Graph databases, or combining vector, full-text, time-series and geospatial retrieval
 Compilers, query language design or cost-based optimizers
 Example projects
 Build a system that retrieves and reasons over everything known about any company or person in the world, answering any factual question precisely and completely.
 Answer precise multi-hop questions over hundreds of billions of claims at thousands of QPS with interactive latency.
 Build a planner that picks the right mix of graph, vector, full-text and geospatial retrieval for any question, and proves it chose well.
 Make new knowledge queryable seconds after it's synthesized, without ever serving an inconsistent result.
 Logistics
 Location: This is an in-person opportunity in Zurich.
 Visas: We're happy to sponsor international candidates (e.g., STEM OPT, OPT, H1B, O1, E3). While we cannot guarantee your visa, we have historically been successful in sponsoring candidates from all over the world. If you receive an offer, our team will work hard to get you a visa.
 Benefits: We offer premium healthcare benefits (medical, dental, vision), fertility benefits, 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave for all new parents, and a monthly wellness stipend to all of our employees.

About the Role at RobCo 
 RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works. 
   At RobCo, we automate the ordinary, so humans can do the extraordinary. To achieve this, we are looking for an ambitious Automation, IT Systems & Security Specialist (m/f/d) to help us establish RobCo as leading provider of automation solutions.
 In this key role, you act as the architect and guardian of our internal IT infrastructure. Your focus is not on maintaining the status quo, but on building a highly secure, automated, and scalable system landscape. You eliminate manual effort through intelligent IT automation and ensure that our network and security architecture keeps pace with our global growth.
 Your Responsibilities 
 Design and implementation of a secure, cloud-aligned IT and network landscape (e.g. AWS, Zero Trust principles)
 Ensuring highest standards in Identity & Access Management (IAM), SSO, and secrets management
 Protection of endpoints and continuous monitoring of system integrity across all teams
 Identification and automation of repetitive IT processes (e.g. automated onboarding/offboarding, asset management)
 Selection and integration of tools that connect and streamline internal workflows across Finance, HR, and Engineering
 Active use of modern automation tools, including AI-supported solutions, to sustainably reduce manual support effort
 Ownership of global device and lifecycle management, including rollout processes
 Acting as a technical lead for complex first- and second-level support topics
 Close collaboration with Engineering and Cloud teams on infrastructure, security, and automation topics
 We're looking for someone who has: 
 Completed vocational training or a degree in Computer Science, IT Systems, Security or a comparable field
 Several years of experience in system administration, network architecture, or IT security in cloud environments
 Strong ownership mindset: you take responsibility, proactively identify gaps, and close them independently
 A strong automation mindset: you are driven by the principle of not doing things twice manually and actively use scripting or tools to improve processes
 Deep understanding of cloud architectures, modern identity models, and network security concepts
 A structured and pragmatic working style, combined with a strong ownership mindset and focus on scalable systems
 Very good English skills (German is a plus)
 Why join RobCo? 
 Develop modular, software-defined robotics solutions with us that set new standards in automation.
 Help us build robots equipped with state-of-the-art AI that perceive their environment, analyze data, and make intelligent decisions in real time.
 As part of a very dynamic and fast-growing scale-up, you will take on responsibility from day one, drive your own projects, and see the direct impact of your work.
 Flat hierarchies, open communication, and regular 360° feedback enable fast decisions and support your professional and personal development.
 Work out across Germany in over 7,200 studios with our subsidized Wellpass membership.
 Flexible working hours, a modern office, and—depending on the role—the option to work from home.
 Regular team events—from relaxed beer & pizza nights on the rooftop terrace to shared experiences on ski trips or at Oktoberfest.
 About RobCo 
 Founded in Munich in 2020, RobCo leads the transition toward fully Autonomous Industrial Robotics. Our mission is to deploy RobCo in every factory - solving the industrial labor shortage through end-to-end robotics that just works. Powered by Physical AI, our solutions combine a scalable modular hardware architecture with intelligent software that continuously learns and improves, requiring zero upfront investment through our Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model.
 We solve our customers' most pressing pain points - labor shortage, cost pressure, workplace safety, and national reshoring - across the full spectrum of Autonomous Industrial Robotics. In October 2026, RobCo reached unicorn status with a valuation exceeding one billion US dollars, with its valuation doubling in less than nine months. With $200M raised from investors including Sequoia, Lightspeed, Lingotto, Kindred, Cherry Ventures, and the European Tech Collective, 225+ people globally, and 3.5M+ operating hours in the field, we are deploying robots in factories across Europe and the United States - with our US operations headquartered in Austin, TX, and our Bay Area Lab in San Francisco.
 Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles. 
 At RobCo, applicants are selected regardless of ethnic origin, religion, gender, age, disability, or sexual orientation. All decisions throughout the recruitment process are based solely on applicants’ qualifications, skills, knowledge, and experience, as well as relevant business requirements.

 The role 
 We're looking for a Staff Backend Engineer to join Stream on our mission of elevating the quality of apps for billions of users globally. You'll own the technical direction of Stream Video's media plane and the infrastructure it runs on.

 What you'll work on 
 Stream Video runs on an SFU we built in Go on top of Pion, plus ingest and recording fleets, all on a global edge network we own across more than one cloud. Our central infrastructure team is tuned for request-based services, and video breaks in different ways: live sessions can't be dropped, bandwidth is the biggest cost, and placement is the main lever.  Job responsibilities: 
 Architecture: write the architecture and roadmap for Stream Video's backend and media infrastructure, and decide what ships.

 Gate production changes: define the validation that decides which changes, including AI-generated ones, reach live media, using behaviour tests on realistic networks, nightly telemetry scans and a public quality benchmark.
 Take the final escalation: handle the hardest quality, latency and production incidents, and work with enterprise customers on advanced integrations.
 Raise the bar: mentor senior engineers through design review, code review and hiring.
 About you 
 You've owned systems where a dropped session or a bad rollout is visible to users within seconds, and you think about cost and reliability as much as features.
